title: LogDrawer
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll, MonarchMethodBadge, MonarchDescriptionList (with its MonarchCopyButton), MonarchBadge, MonarchCodeBlock and MonarchButton; android.text.format.DateUtils for the time
summary: A recipe, not a component: the full record of one log entry (an API request, a webhook delivery, a job run) in a bottom sheet, with method and path, status, request ID with copy, time, duration and the payload.
whenToUse: When a row of a request log, webhook log or job list is tapped and the person needs every detail of that one entry.
whenNotToUse: For the streaming output of a run use MonarchLogViewer. For a short summary that fits in the row, leave it in the list.
api: MonarchText(text = "Request details", style = MonarchTextStyle.Heading, heading = true)
MonarchDescriptionList(items = listOf(MonarchDescriptionItem("Status", "502") { MonarchBadge(text = "502", tone = statusTone(502)) }, MonarchDescriptionItem("Request ID", id, copyable = true), …))

options.name: entry
options.description: The log entry: method, path, status, request ID, time in epoch milliseconds, duration and payload.

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the sheet is shown; set it from the row's tap and clear it in onDismissRequest and Close.

options.name: statusTone
options.description: Success for 2xx, info for 3xx, warning for 4xx and danger for 5xx, as the web's httpStatusTone.

states.name: closed
states.description: Only the list or button that opens the sheet.

states.name: open
states.description: A modal bottom sheet, half height and pulled to full height, titled "Request details", with Close at the end.

states.name: loading
states.description: While the entry loads, show MonarchLoadingState with the Detail variant and the label "Loading details" in the sheet.

states.name: load error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with "The details did not load." and Try again in the sheet.

states.name: status tones
states.description: The status badge uses success for 2xx, info for 3xx, warning for 4xx and danger for 5xx, with the code as its text.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the sheet's surface: a heading, the method badge and the path in the code type, a stacked description list, a toned status badge, the code block and a full-width button. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships LogDrawer as one component: a side sheet from the right that fills the screen on phones, with request, fields, loading, error, onRetry, locale, now and messages props. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe: a modal bottom sheet is the phone's surface for one record's details, and each fact is a MonarchDescriptionItem the app lists itself, leaving out the facts the entry does not have. The web's httpStatusTone helper is a small function in the recipe. There is no relative time with a tooltip; write the time with DateUtils (minSdk 24, no java.time). On a large screen the same content can go in MonarchResponsiveDialog or a supporting pane.
accessibility: The sheet is modal for TalkBack and Back closes it; the title has heading semantics.
Each fact of MonarchDescriptionList is read as the term and the value.
The request ID's copy button is named "Copy Request ID" and announces the copy.
The status is a word in a badge, not only a color.
Close is a 48dp MonarchButton at the end of the content.
edgeCases: Long paths wrap in the code type; the payload code block scrolls sideways inside itself or wraps with its toggle.
Leave out a fact the entry does not have instead of showing an empty value.
At the largest text sizes the content scrolls inside the sheet; pull the sheet to full height.
